statement: To the extent the aggregate fair market value of stock with respect to which incentive stock options are exercisable for the first time by an individual during any calendar year (across all plans of the employer and related corporations) exceeds $100,000, the options are treated as nonstatutory options (26 U.S.C. § 422(d)); fair market value is determined as of the grant date, options are taken into account in the order granted (§ 422(d)(2)–(3)), and a single option may be treated in part as an ISO and in part as a nonstatutory option (Treas. Reg. § 1.422-4(b)). Acceleration of exercisability (e.g. on a change in control) pulls options into the year they first become exercisable (Reg. § 1.422-4(d) Example 3).
caveat: The regulation's full rules (disregarded options, cancellation timing, stock designation on bifurcation, employer aggregation) have facts this repo does not verify; plan documents often also self-limit. The $100,000 figure is statutory and not inflation-indexed, but verify current law before relying on it.
